name: narrow-zone-band
rationale: The zone boundaries (hold_jpy_below=0.2 / hold_btc_above=0.8) have never been moved, and they are unreachable in practice. Simulator::run passes an empty news slice (src/backtest/simulator.rs:92), so sentiment_normalized is pinned at 0.5 and the combined signal can only span [0.15, 0.85] at the baseline's ta_weight=0.7; zone A (all-JPY) therefore needs ta_normalized < 0.0714 and zone C (all-BTC) needs ta_normalized > 0.9286, i.e. essentially all five sub-signals saturated in the same direction. The 2026-09-08 run tested the other way of removing that compression -- full-ta-weight-no-sentiment set ta_weight=1.0 -- and it was rejected (Sharpe -0.674, drawdown +0.62pp), but that variant also changed what the signal means, not just where the decision boundaries sit. This hypothesis leaves the weights alone and narrows the band instead (0.35 / 0.65), which both makes the extreme zones reachable under the real [0.15, 0.85] range and roughly doubles the slope of the interpolation in between, so a given signal move produces a larger allocation move. That directly targets the trend the last three runs recorded: turnover has fallen 37 -> 34 -> 25 trades per 14-day holdout (2.6 -> 2.4 -> 1.79 trades/day) against a 4-10/day guideline, with allocations clustering mid-zone.
